idiom_name: PORO service object with one public #call and constructor-injected collaborators (module_function for stateless helpers)
implementation_notes: Ruby's service object is a plain class: collaborators come in as keyword arguments to initialize with sensible defaults, the work happens in a single public method conventionally named call, and the result is a rich result object or Struct rather than a boolean. Ruby has no interface keyword, so the contract is duck-typed - any object responding to the same messages substitutes, and a module with module_function replaces the class when the operation needs no collaborators. Keep Active Record out of the service: the caller (controller or application service) owns the transaction, and dry-transaction/railway style is available when a multi-step process is the real problem.
code_sketch:
# app/services/payments/charge_customer.rb
module Payments
  class ChargeCustomer
    Result = Struct.new(:success?, :charge_id, keyword_init: true)

    def initialize(gateway: PaymentGateway.new) = @gateway = gateway  # injected

    def call(customer, amount)                         # one public method
      Result.new(success?: true, charge_id: @gateway.charge(customer.token, amount).id)
    end
  end
end
pitfalls: Class methods (def self.call) are global symbols: they cannot be substituted in tests and invite VM-wide state; prefer instance methods behind .new.
Assigning to instance variables mid-operation makes behaviour depend on how often the same service instance is reused - assign locals and return a result instead.
Reaching for Active Record scopes inside the service turns it into a query object and mixes persistence into the domain rule; keep persistence behind a repository.
